title: Constraint-aware prompt ensemble notes
body:
Quick brain-dump: idea = run small ensemble of template variants and enforce a short constraints pipeline (token budget, banned-phrases, answer-shape) before returning.

Motivation:
- Many brittle failures come from a single template producing a seemingly plausible but forbidden output (PII, hallucination).
- Instead of heavy reranking or a large safety model, use a lightweight constraint layer + ensemble voting to increase robustness with minimal latency hit.

Core components (sketch):
1) Template pool (3–6 variants): short, verbose, instructive, role-primed, context-windowed.  Keep each template limited to ~60 tokens preamble.
2) Few-shot exemplars: 2–4 examples tailored to the requested task class.  Exemplar selection based on nearest-context heuristics (embedding cosine) not random.
3) Constraint layer: quick post-process checks (string-level and model-lite checks):
   - token budget check (reject candidate if > allowed tokens)
   - banned-phrases list (canned sensitive phrases)
   - output shape regex (e.g., JSON or list)
   - simple factuality probe: ask short yes/no followup to a small internal verifier model (low cost)
4) Aggregation: score candidates (pass/fail constraints, coherence score, length penalty) and pick top; fallback to safe-summary template on failure.

Notes / heuristics tried so far (tests):
- Prompt variant A: "You are a succinct assistant. Answer strictly in plain text. If uncertain, say \"I don't know.\""  -> high brevity, but high hallucination when context sparse.
- Prompt variant B: role-play with chain-of-thought suppressed: good for factual Q/A but verbose.
- Few-shot set S1 (2 examples) focused on negative examples (showing what not to do) seems to reduce hallucination more than positive-only examples.  Strange but repeated in 3 runs.

Failure cases observed:
- When exemplars are borderline-relevant (similar domain but different intent), ensemble increases variance rather than consensus.  Need better exemplar filtering.
- Banned-phrases check sometimes too strict: blocks legitimate domain tokens (e.g., medical shorthand).  Add allowlist by tag.
- Verifier false positives: short verifier sometimes marks correct facts as unknown due to prompt mismatch.  Consider using same model family for verifier or calibration set.

Quick templates (live experiments):
- T_short:
"""
You are a concise assistant. Use at most 50 words. Answer the user query directly. If you cannot answer, reply: \"I don't know\".
"""
- T_structured:
"""
You are an assistant that must respond in JSON: {"answer": ..., "confidence": "low|medium|high"}. Provide a one-sentence answer and a confidence level. If unsure, set confidence to low and answer: \"I don't know\".
"""
- T_explain_then_answer:
"""
First, in one line, write the key assumption you made. Then provide the answer. Keep the whole response under 120 tokens.
"""

Few-shot seeds (for classification-to-answer tasks):
Example 1: Q: "Is insulin required for type 2 diabetes?" A: "Sometimes — depends on progression; consult a clinician."
Example 2: Q: "Can ibuprofen be taken with warfarin?" A: "No — there is increased bleeding risk; verify with pharmacist."

Evaluation plan:
- Automatic metrics: hallucination rate (via ground-truth pairs where available), average token cost, pass-rate of constraints, consensus rate across ensemble.
- Human spot checks: 50 random queries across 5 domains (legal, medical, finance, dev, general knowledge).
- A/B: baseline single-template vs ensemble constrained pipeline. Track latency 50/95/99 percentiles.

TODOs (near term):
- [ ] Implement exemplar nearest-neighbor filter by embeddings and a simple threshold.
- [ ] Add configurable allowlist per customer tag to bypass banned-phrases for domain tokens.
- [ ] Build lightweight verifier harness (reuse small 7B family we already host).
- [ ] Run 1k query smoke tests across open QA datasets (SQuAD-style, consumer health QA) and capture failure taxonomy.

Open questions / hypotheses to test:
- H1: Small ensemble (3 templates) + constraints will reduce hallucination rate by ~15% with <10% latency overhead.
- H2: Negative exemplars (show what not to do) consistently reduce confident hallucinations more than additional positive exemplars.
- H3: A verifier from the same model family reduces false positives vs a different-family verifier.

Notes-to-self: keep template wording intentionally varied (imperative vs conversational vs role) — diversity seems to help voting.  Also track per-template calibration (confidence distribution) to weight votes.

Link stash: put experimental scripts under github PR above; keep results CSVs in a nested drive folder when available (will move to shared_drives if promising).

Experimental run log snippets:
- 2025-02-05: 200 queries (mixed domains) -> ensemble pass-rate 78%, baseline 62%; median latency +12ms.
- 2025-02-20: verifier false-positive spike when exemplar domain mismatch increased; adjust exemplar threshold.

End of note.

Quick filename idea for next doc: "ensemble-exemplar-filtering-experiments" - keep separate run logs per date.

(Notes intentionally rough; tidy before sharing.)
